shortTitle: Inverted Y & Five Triangles: Posterior Groin Anatomy
title: Systemization of laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair (TAPP) based on a new anatomical concept: inverted Y and five triangles
citation: Furtado M, Claus C, Malcher F, Cavazzola LT, Felix E. (2019).
learningObjectives: Identify the three structures that form the Inverted Y in the posterior view.
Name the Five Triangles and state what each contains at a high level.
Use the framework to orient yourself immediately after peritoneal opening in TAPP/rTAPP.
paperIn3MinBullets: Defines a reproducible posterior-view anatomy map for TAPP based on the ‘Inverted Y’ and ‘Five Triangles’.
Uses three landmark structures (inferior epigastrics, vas deferens, gonadal vessels) to orient the field quickly.
Divides the posterior groin into triangles to standardize where dissection is performed and where danger structures live.
Intended as a teaching and standardization tool to reduce cognitive overload early in the learning curve.
Pairs laparoscopic images with schematic overlays to reinforce spatial layout.

activities.title: Posterior groin overview (overlays OFF by default)
activities.instructions: Start with overlays OFF. Turn on Inverted Y, then triangles. Keep labels minimal: names only.

activities.title: Name the triangles
activities.prompt: Select the correct triangle name for the highlighted region.

activities.title: Which zone are you in?
activities.prompt: Based on the highlighted region, which dissection zone is this?
activities.explanation: Use the paper’s zone concept to mentally bucket risk and attention.

flashcards.front: Inverted Y: name the 3 structures that form it.
flashcards.back: Inferior epigastric vessels (superior limb) + vas deferens (medial limb) + gonadal/spermatic vessels (lateral limb).

flashcards.front: Why use the Inverted Y early in TAPP/rTAPP?
flashcards.back: Fast orientation after peritoneal opening; anchors the rest of the posterior anatomy map.
Partition the posterior groin into consistent regions so you can predict what structures live where and standardize dissection.

quiz.q: The Inverted Y is formed by which set of structures?
choices: Vas deferens, Cooper’s ligament, iliopubic tract
Inferior epigastrics, vas deferens, gonadal vessels
External iliac vein, femoral nerve, corona mortis
quiz.explanation: The Inverted Y is the key orientation tool described in the paper.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of the Five Triangles framework?
choices: To organize posterior-view anatomy into predictable regions
quiz.explanation: It’s a spatial organization tool for posterior groin anatomy.

quiz.q: In this module, why are overlays OFF by default?
choices: To force the learner to orient visually before relying on guides
quiz.explanation: Orientation is the dominant cognitive task; overlays are scaffolding.

quiz.q: Best use of this paper during learning TAPP/rTAPP is:
choices: Build a mental map immediately after peritoneal opening
quiz.explanation: It is primarily an orientation framework.

quiz.q: This module intentionally avoids which activity?
choices: Safety hypotheticals and operative decision drills
quiz.explanation: Furtado module is the map; decision-making is emphasized in Yasukawa.
